guardian.description:
Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda

Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said.

The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola. It is unclear when she arrived in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country.

Mitchell Fairbarn found guilty of animal cruelty after prosecutors say he hurt and frightened the 27-year-old bird

A Canadian man was convicted of animal cruelty charges on Monday for snatching a flamingo named Peachy from its enclosure at an iconic Las Vegas hotel.

Prosecutors said it was a malicious prank while a lawyer for the tourist insisted it was drunken foolishness not meant to harm the bird.

rfi.title: France mobilises 70,000 police and gendarmes for Saturday protests
rfi.description: France will deploy some 70,000 police officers and gendarmes nationwide during a fresh round of protests this weekend, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said on Friday, as President Emmanuel Macron met with student organisations at the Élysée Palace for the first time since the high school protests started more than a month ago.

rfi.title: Deadly shooting west of Paris ‘clearly terrorist’ attack, interior minister says
rfi.description: One person was killed and four others were wounded, including a 12-year-old girl, when shots were fired from a car in two suburbs west of Paris on Friday. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the shooting was “clearly a terrorist crime” and “a racist, probably Islamophobic attack”.

rfi.title: ‘Too arrogant, too sure of itself’ France confronts its legacy in Africa
rfi.description: Fifteen years after France promised a new relationship with Africa, Paris is still struggling to reconcile its rejection of colonial-era interference with its desire to retain influence on the continent. RFI Africa specialist Christophe Boisbouvier argues in a new book that France can still build a partnership of equals – based on respect rather than arrogance or domination.

rfi.title: Casualties feared as multi-storey building collapses in Nairobi
rfi.description: A multi-storey building collapsed mid-construction in the Kenyan capital on Friday, with many feared trapped in the rubble and accusations of dangerous building work.

rfi.title: Student-led movement seeks to unseat ruling party in Serbian election
rfi.description: Serbia's student-led protest movement is mounting its biggest challenge yet to former president Aleksandar Vucic, as voters prepare to elect a new parliament on Sunday after nearly two years of demonstrations against alleged corruption.

rfi.title: Orléans tightens security ahead of far-right National Rally party congress
rfi.description: Orléans says it will impose exceptional security measures ahead of the far-right National Rally's congress this weekend, when counter-demonstrations against "racism, fascism and imperialism" could drawn up to 25,000 people.

rfi.title: Kenya searches for missing Ugandan contact as Ebola cases rise
rfi.description: Kenyan authorities are searching for a Ugandan national who came into contact with the country's first Ebola patient in Nairobi, as the number of confirmed cases linked to the initial cluster rises to nine.

rfi.title: International Criminal Court wins EU's Sakharov human rights prize
rfi.description: Facing US sanctions, the International Criminal Court was on Thursday awarded the European Union's top rights prize, in a show of support that risks upsetting President Donald Trump.

rfi.title: Bill to make vandals pay for damage advances in wake of France's unrest
rfi.description: France has taken a further step towards making people financially responsible for damage they cause during urban riots in the wake of last weekend's unrest, when largely peaceful demonstrations over the cost of living were marred by widespread looting and destruction of public property.

rfi.title: Nearly all coral reefs at risk of collapse by 2075, conservation body warns
rfi.description: Nearly all of the world's shallow-water coral reefs face an extremely high risk of collapse within the next 50 years due to climate change, the International Union for Conservation of Nature, the the world's authority on endangered wildlife warned on Thursday.

rfi.title: Senegal unions press on with general strike days before Youth Olympics
rfi.description: Senegal’s three-day general strike entered its second day on Thursday, with unions pressing the government to honour agreements on pay, pensions and working conditions amid a deepening economic crisis. The action comes just days before Senegal hosts the Youth Olympic Games.

rfi.title: Websites go dark as AI exposes critical security flaws worldwide
rfi.description: Governments and companies around the world shut down websites as they raced Thursday to protect themselves from hacks after artificial intelligence uncovered critical flaws in a widely used programming language called PHP.

rfi.title: Cameroon's Eseka rail disaster survivors still waiting for justice, 10 years on
rfi.description: A decade after Cameroon’s deadliest rail disaster killed 79 people and injured more than 500, survivors are still living with serious injuries, some compensation remains unpaid and an appeal against the convictions over the crash has yet to be heard. RFI spoke to survivors still living with the consequences of the disaster and to the husband of a woman whose body has never been found.

rfi.title: World set to breach 1.5C warming limit as UN warns time is running out
rfi.description: Global warming is now set to breach the 1.5C target limit set out in the 2015 Paris Agreement, after decades of insufficient climate action, the United Nations Environment Programme has warned. Temperatures could still be reduced, but only with far larger emissions cuts and the removal of vast amounts of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere using methods the UN says are "costly and risky".

rfi.title: Rescuers search for French air force navigator after jet pilot dies in crash
rfi.description: Rescue teams were on Wednesday searching north-eastern France for the navigator of a French air force jet, after the pilot died in a crash on Tuesday night in bad weather.

rfi.title: PSG's Kvaratskhelia season in doubt after torn ACL
rfi.description: Paris Saint-Germain could be without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for the rest of the season after the winger tore his ACL in the Champions League win against Barcelona and Ousmane Dembélé faces weeks out too, the club said on Wednesday.

rfi.title: PSG boss Enrique plays down perfect start to defence of Champions League crown
rfi.description: Paris Saint-Germain head coach Luis Enrique on Wednesday played down his side's winning start to the defence of their Champions League title, after they clinched their third victory in three games with a 4-2 win over Barcelona at the Parc des Princes.

rfi.title: France turns page on Code Noir as Parliament approves symbolic repeal
rfi.description: France’s Parliament has unanimously approved the symbolic repeal of the Code Noir and related legislation governing slavery in its former colonies, closing a legal chapter left formally unresolved since abolition in 1848.

euronews.title: Hungary: 70 years after Soviet crackdown, leaders honour uprising victims
euronews.description: Seventy years after Hungary's 1956 uprising against Soviet rule, Prime Minister Péter Magyar paid tribute to its victims as Ursula von der Leyen highlighted the importance of freedom and democracy.

euronews.title: Princess and prizewinners champion hope against 'darker times' at Princess of Asturias Awards
euronews.description: The heiress to the throne quoted Paul Valéry through a Studio Ghibli character – "The wind rises, we must try to live!" – to conclude a strongly political speech about combating contemporary disillusionment, a theme echoed in several of the other winners' speeches.

euronews.title: Jihadists reportedly urge attacks during protests in Portugal and Spain
euronews.description: Spanish newspaper El País has obtained what it identifies as an Interior Ministry report detailing calls for attacks on police officers and protesters during weeks-long demonstrations in several European countries.

euronews.title: US designates helium as critical material as Europe faces supply squeeze
euronews.description: The US has declared helium a critical material as war in the Middle East and export curbs by Russia and China squeeze global supplies of a gas vital to chipmaking, leaving Europe scrambling to secure its share.

euronews.title: Italy preparing with elite troops and drone surveillance for 24 October protests
euronews.description: On 24 October Rome will be locked down with 1,500 officers, Milan with 1,800 police and soldiers.

euronews.title: Meghan Markle 'distressed' by child abuse image allegations against father
euronews.description: Markle has been estranged from her father since 2018, when he was caught staging paparazzi photos in the run-up to her wedding to Harry.

euronews.title: Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany hospitalised after collapse during training
euronews.description: A few weeks ago, sporting director Max Eberl said that Kompany, who reportedly needed help climbing stairs, had been struggling with both a viral infection and a hip injury.

euronews.title: A year ahead of the ‘wrecking ball’: Scientists find new clue to predict when El Niño will strike
euronews.description: Predicting El Niño a year in advance could help communities and decision makers better prepare for the weather phenomenon's impact.

euronews.title: France bolsters security as businesses fear renewed unrest during Saturday protests
euronews.description: A massive security operation has been deployed across France for major protests on Saturday. Businesses across the country remain tense following violence which overshadowed peaceful demonstrations last weekend.

euronews.title: UN chief race enters decisive phase as new contender arrives
euronews.description: UAE’s star diplomat Lana Nusseibeh has entered the race for the UN secretary-general position, challenging front-runner Rebeca Grynspan at a decisive time for the global organisation's future. The UN chief race could now lead to the first ever female secretary-general.

euronews.title: EU trade Chief seeks to rebalance EU-China trade as Brussels weighs tougher measures
euronews.description: The European Commission hopes to curb Chinese imports in additional sectors in upcoming talks with Beijing while exploring new trade defence measures, though the move risks triggering retaliatory action from China.

euronews.title: Studio DRIFT makes the invisible force of wind visible in stunning new London installation
euronews.description: Amsterdam-based art studio DRIFT has unveiled Aeolus, a large-scale installation at London’s Ladbroke Hall that uses hundreds of glass rods and hidden lights to make the invisible movement of wind visible.

euronews.title: EU vies to expand role in Ukraine-Russia peace talks to influence US thinking
euronews.description: Brussels wants to turn the next round of trilateral peace talks betwen Ukraine, Russia and the US into a multilateral format with European representation.

euronews.title: Kenya: huge piles of rubble after high-rise building collapses
euronews.description: A multi-storey building under construction has collapsed in Nairobi, leaving a vast pile of rubble. Red Cross workers have arrived at the scene, where excavators are being used among the debris.

euronews.title: CICA members look to turn regional dialogue into action
euronews.description: The Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) brought together member states to discuss regional security, economic cooperation and shared challenges, with a focus on strengthening the organisation's role and turning dialogue into practical action.

euronews.title: Melania Trump secures ceasefire in Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, White House says
euronews.description: The agreement, due to take effect on 29 October, is intended to allow humanitarian aid and civilian evacuations in a city where residents have endured years of Russian occupation, severe food shortages and dangerous attempts to escape.

euronews.title: First human case of cattle virus Shamonda: How worried should Europe be? EU agency explains
euronews.description: The first human case of Shamonda virus, confirmed in France, poses no wider threat to Europeans, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) told Euronews.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, tirs à Trappes et à La Verrière : « Ce qu’il s’est passé aujourd’hui est un tournant dans la vie de notre République », déclare Emmanuel Macron, qui dénonce un « attentat terroriste raciste »
lemonde.description: Le Parquet national antiterroriste a fait savoir, vendredi dans la soirée, que le tireur avait piégé son appartement avec trois bouteilles de gaz et des fils électriques. Il a été interpellé et placé en garde à vue. Un membre de son entourage a également été placé en garde à vue.

lemonde.title: Mobilisation du 24 octobre : un dispositif policier conséquent, mais pas hors du commun
lemonde.description: Le ministre de l’intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, a indiqué que 70 000 policiers et gendarmes seront mobilisés sur le terrain, samedi, sans compter les unités susceptibles d’être sollicitées, comme le RAID ou le GIGN. C’est 10 000 effectifs de plus que le 17 octobre.

lemonde.title: Congrès du RN : Orléans se prépare à être l’épicentre de mobilisations d’ampleur
lemonde.description: De 20 000 à 30 000 opposants sont attendus en marge du congrès du Rassemblement national, samedi 24 octobre. De nombreux commerces seront fermés et les transports à l’arrêt dans une ville mise sous cloche.

lemonde.title: L’agence Moody’s maintient la note souveraine de la France à Aa3, mais y assortit une perspective négative
lemonde.description: Cette décision « déjoue les pronostics déclinistes de nombreux “experts” et de ceux qui spéculent sur la dette française », a salué le premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu.

lemonde.title: Une « belle élection présidentielle » en 2027 est-elle possible malgré l’éruption sociale ?
lemonde.description: Depuis les violences en marge des manifestations du 17 octobre, l’engrenage de la surenchère s’est enclenché, interrogeant notre capacité à débattre sereinement de la prochaine échéance électorale pourtant cruciale, analyse Matthieu Goar, l’un des chefs du service Politique du « Monde ».

lemonde.title: La diplomatie de Giorgia Meloni, une politique au cœur de l’internationale réactionnaire
lemonde.description: « Meloni, quatre années au pouvoir » (5/6). La présidente du conseil italien, d’extrême droite, cultive ses affinités idéologiques avec les dirigeants les plus conservateurs, comme Donald Trump, Javier Milei ou Viktor Orban. Et œuvre en Europe, grâce à ses réseaux, au durcissement de la lutte contre l’immigration illégale.

lemonde.title: Cisjordanie : en réponse à une attaque contre des militaires israéliens, Nétanyahou promet des destructions d’ampleur et encore plus de colonies
lemonde.description: Après la mort de deux soldats près d’Hébron, le premier ministre israélien a promis « une opération très vaste de l’armée », mais l’état-major semble plus modéré, à quatre jours d’élections législatives décisives.

lemonde.title: Budget de la « Sécu » : les députés sabordent le projet de loi à l’Assemblée nationale
lemonde.description: Dans un hémicycle quasiment déserté par les soutiens du gouvernement, les députés ont rejeté la partie « recettes » du projet de loi de financement de la Sécurité sociale. Le parcours du texte n’est pas terminé et le gouvernement espère encore trouver une voie de passage.

lemonde.title: Jean-Paul Huchon ou l’art du compromis, de Rocard à la région Ile-de-France
lemonde.description: Figure influente du Parti socialiste, ce rocardien historique, décédé vendredi, a régné dix-sept ans sur la région francilienne.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : l’armée ukrainienne dit qu’elle observera une trêve à Olechky à partir de mardi pour permettre des opérations humanitaires
lemonde.description: La Maison Blanche avait annoncé que Moscou et Kiev avaient « accepté de suspendre temporairement toutes les opérations militaires dans cette ville afin de permettre l’acheminement de l’aide humanitaire et de préparer l’évacuation des civils par un couloir sécurisé désigné à cet effet ».

lemonde.title: Derrière la condamnation d’Olivier Bouygues, « un sérieux avertissement pour les grands propriétaires de domaines de chasse »
lemonde.description: L’homme d’affaires a été condamné à deux ans de prison avec sursis et 750 000 euros d’amende pour l’abattage, par ses gardes-chasse, d’espèces protégées sur sa propriété solognote. Il a fait appel.

lemonde.title: Oraux de médecine : pas de « fraude massive » mais la triche reste possible, selon les inspections générales
lemonde.description: Dans un rapport publié le 23 octobre, aucune faille de sécurité systémique majeure n’a été identifiée lors des épreuves orales du concours de l’internat. La mission d’inspection alerte toutefois sur des fragilités rendant possible la fraude. Mi-septembre, un étudiant anonyme avait affirmé détenir les preuves d’une triche à grande échelle.

lemonde.title: Les Forges de Tarbes, producteurs des corps d’obus du canon Caesar, demandent leur placement en redressement judiciaire
lemonde.description: « Cette demande vise à préserver l’activité de l’entreprise », a fait savoir le groupe Europlasma dans un communiqué publié jeudi soir, quelques heures après en avoir informé les représentants des salariés lors d’un CSE extraordinaire.

lemonde.title: Roumanie : deux attaques au couteau, dont l’une en lien avec la mouvance True Crime Community, ont fait quatre blessés dans des écoles
lemonde.description: En moins d’une semaine, deux agressions à l’arme blanche ont eu lieu dans deux établissements roumains. L’un des auteurs serait lié à la communauté en ligne TCC glorifiant la violence extrême et qui aurait influencé le passage à l’acte de l’adolescent  responsable de tirs à Aubagne le 12 octobre.

lemonde.title: La crise dans le Golfe accroît la dépendance au charbon des pays d’Afrique australe
lemonde.description: Le blocage du détroit d’Ormuz a fait grimper les cours du charbon, énergie très polluante mais encore relativement bon marché. Pour les pays exportateurs comme l’Afrique du Sud et le Mozambique, cette hausse est une aubaine, mais elle les éloigne de leurs objectifs en matière de transition énergétique.

lemonde.title: Tempête Austen : trois départements du nord de la France restent en vigilance orange, 242 000 foyers privés d’électricité
lemonde.description: Seuls le Nord, le Pas-de-Calais et la Somme sont toujours placés en vigilance orange pour vent. Un homme est mort en coupant un arbre après le passage de la tempête vendredi dans la Manche.

france24fr.title: Manifestations du 24 octobre : 70 000 policiers et gendarmes déployés, les lycéens toujours mobilisés
france24fr.description: Plusieurs représentants lycéens ont été reçus à l'Élysée vendredi pour échanger avec Emmanuel Macron, à la veille d'une nouvelle journée de contestation qui mobilise plus de 70 000 policiers et gendarmes. Globalement "satisfaits" de l'écoute du président, ils ont néanmoins appelé vendredi à "continuer à se mobiliser" jusqu'à l'annonce de mesures concrètes.

france24fr.title: 🔴 L'agence Moody's maintient la note souveraine de la France à Aa3 avec perspective négative
FC Barcelone vs Real Madrid : un Clásico équilibré ?
france24fr.description: C’est le match que toute la planète foot attend avec impatience : le FC Barcelone reçoit le Real Madrid au Camp Nou dimanche. Allons-nous assister, pour ce match aller, à un Clásico équilibré ?

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis pourraient frapper l'Iran dès ce week-end, avance un diplomate américain
france24fr.description: L'émissaire américain Tom Barrack a déclaré vendredi lors d'un entretien que les États-Unis pourraient frapper l'Iran dès ce week-end. Des propos qui interviennent après de nombreuses menaces en ce sens de Washington et d'Israël ces derniers jours.

france24fr.title: Gabriel Dia à AKAA : l'art, les tabous et l'homosexualité au Sénégal
france24fr.description:
À Paris, la foire d'art contemporain africain AKAA accueille une installation monumentale du photographe sénégalais Gabriel Dia. Avec Mother's Heritage, l'artiste revisite ses souvenirs d'enfance dans l'atelier de couture de sa mère, à Rufisque. Des photographies imprimées sur des tissus suspendus pour raconter la transmission, les interdits et la liberté d'être soi.

De son parcours dans l'ingénierie nucléaire à ses séries photographiques Sabar et Mother's Heritage, Gabriel Dia revient sur une

france24fr.title: Gabon: Ali Bongo revient en politique et revendique la tête du PDG
france24fr.description: Au Gabon, Ali Bongo sort de son silence. Dans une vidéo publiée depuis Paris, l'ancien président gabonais annonce son retour en politique. Son objectif immédiat : reprendre la tête du Parti démocratique gabonais, le PDG. Il conteste désormais son propre retrait de la scène politique, annoncé en septembre 2024, et revendique la légitimité à la direction du parti. Une prise de parole qui secoue Libreville.

france24fr.title: Emmanuel Macron appelle à l'unité après l'attaque "terroriste raciste" de Trappes
france24fr.description: Le président Emmanuel Macron a dénoncé vendredi soir à Trappes un "attentat terroriste raciste" et a appelé à l'unité, après la fusillade survenue dans la matinée, qui a fait un mort et plusieurs blessés. Une enquête a été ouverte par le Parquet national antiterroriste.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : Macron évoque "un tournant" et dénonce un "attentat" commis "sur la base d'une idéologie raciste"
Tirs dans les Yvelines :  le maire dénonce "un attentat à connotation raciste"
france24fr.description: Qualifiant l'attaque meurtrière des Yvelines d'attentat à "connotation raciste" et "objectivement islamophobe", le maire de Trappes, Ali Rabeh, a exhorté vendredi à la "concorde républicaine".

france24fr.title: États-Unis : en Géorgie, les Afro-Américains mobilisés pour les midterms
france24fr.description: C’est l’un des États clés des élections de mi-mandat. En Géorgie, le siège du sénateur démocrate Jon Ossoff est en jeu, et peut-être avec lui la majorité au Sénat. Les Afro-Américains, qui représentent environ un tiers de l’électorat, sont plus courtisés que jamais. Dans les églises comme dans la rue, on les presse de voter tôt. Reportage à Atlanta.

france24fr.title: Violences du 17 octobre : qui va payer l'addition ?
france24fr.description: Après les violences du 17 octobre, près de 3 000 commerces ont été dégradés selon le gouvernement. L’agence Morningstar estime le coût des dégradations à 1,2 milliard d’euros. À Paris, les professionnels du tourisme constatent une hausse des annulations. Le secteur s’inquiète, un phénomène qui pourrait s’accentuer si les débordements se poursuivent. Alors, qui va payer l’addition ? Faiza Younsi en discute avec Pierre Talamon, Philippe Crevel, Laurent Frajerman et Olivier Moustacakis.

france24fr.title: Circonstances, suspect, mobile... ce que l'on sait sur l'attaque "terroriste raciste" à Trappes
france24fr.description: À Trappes puis à La Verrière, dans les Yvelines, un homme a tiré en rafales sur la voie publique depuis son véhicule, tuant une personne et faisant cinq blessés, vendredi. Pour le ministre de l'Intérieur, intervenu sur place, il s'agit d'une attaque terroriste. Que sait-on sur les circonstances de la fusillade et le profil du suspect ? France 24 fait le point.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : Macron à Trappes après les tirs meurtriers, l'Élysée dénonce un "attentat terroriste raciste"
Clément Beaune : “La Chine pose une question de vie ou de mort à l’industrie européenne”
france24fr.description: Nous recevons Clément Beaune, ancien conseiller spécial du Président Emmanuel Macron puis secrétaire d’État aux Affaires européennes, ancien ministre des Transports et désormais Haut-commissaire à la Stratégie et au Plan. Il vient de diriger l’ouvrage Comment vivrons-nous en France demain ? paru le 8 octobre aux éditions Tallandier. Il évoque le rôle de l’Union Européenne dans le soutien à l’Ukraine, la concurrence économique chinoise ou encore les mouvements sociaux qui agitent le continent.

france24fr.title: Droit de manifester en France : "Ce n’est pas au président de choisir ses opposants"
france24fr.description: Suivant la consigne d’Emmanuel Macron, désireux d’éviter de nouvelles scènes de chaos semblables à celles du 17 octobre, de nombreux préfets ont interdit ou drastiquement limité les manifestations prévues samedi en France. Les défenseurs des libertés fondamentales y voient une attaque contre l’État de droit. France 24 fait le point avec Serge Slama, professeur de droit public.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : après leur rencontre avec Macron, des représentants lycéens appellent à poursuivre la mobilisation
Claude Monet : « Iris » devient l’œuvre d’art la plus chère vendue aux enchères en France
france24fr.description: Le tableau "Iris", peint par Claude Monet à la fin de sa vie, a été vendu aux enchères pour 50 millions d'euros jeudi 22 octobre à Paris. Ce tableau de grandes dimensions était présenté au public pour la première fois et avait été estimé entre 22 et 30 millions d'euros avant la vente.

france24fr.title: De Paris à Tirana, en passant par Milan et Athènes, la Gen Z se révolte en Europe
france24fr.description: Les images des scènes de pillages, d’incendies et de violences en marge des manifestations du 17 octobre en France contre la vie chère ont fait le tour du monde. Mairies incendiées, commerces pillés ont occulté une colère, celle d’une jeunesse. Lycéens et étudiants dénoncent un manque de moyens et aussi plus largement une absence de perspective. Le mouvement a fait tache d’huile en Europe, avec des mobilisations en Italie, en Grèce, en Belgique.

zeit.title: Berggasthof: Auf 1.834 Metern Höhe: Kehlsteinhaus in Berchtesgaden brennt
Formel 1: Antonelli nach Wackelsitz knapp geschlagen
Regierungsbildung: Thierse für unabhängigen Regierungschef in Berlin
Künstliche Intelligenz: Nach Hacks: OpenAI will Spitzen-KI ohne Internet trainieren
Unwetter: Sturm wirft Bäume in Duisburg um - einer fällt auf Kiosk
Unfälle: 82-jähriger Autofahrer prallt gegen Baum und stirbt
Bundesliga, 7. Spieltag – Freitag: Borussia Mönchengladbach gewinnt gegen den VfB Stuttgart
zeit.description: Nach sechs Niederlagen hat Mönchengladbach sein erstes Spiel der Bundesligasaison gewonnen. Überraschend schlugen die Borussen den VfB Stuttgart. Der Spielbericht

zeit.title: Senatswahl in Alaska: Trump initiiert Klage gegen Alaska wegen ähnlicher Kandidatennamen
zeit.description: In Alaska konkurrieren zwei Republikaner mit dem Nachnamen Sullivan um einen Sitz im Senat. US-Präsident Trump gefällt das nicht: Er befürchtet Stimmverluste.

zeit.title: CSU-Parteitag in München: Wenn alles im Chaos versinkt, blüht Markus Söder erst so richtig auf
zeit.description: Markus Söder schwört die CSU beim Parteitag auf den demokratischen Nahkampf gegen Radikale ein. Und man sieht, wie er doch noch Kanzler werden könnte.

zeit.title: DDR: Zeitzeugin Sibylle Havemann ist tot
zeit.description: Sibylle Havemann ist im Alter von 71 Jahren gestorben. Die DDR-Zeitzeugin hatte erst im Frühjahr mit der ZEIT über ihre Krebserkrankung gesprochen.

zeit.title: Strategische Ölreserven: Deutschland gibt Öl aus strategischen Reserven frei
zeit.description: Die Bundesregierung hat einen Teil der nationalen Ölreserve freigegeben. Darauf hatte sich die G7 zuvor geeinigt, um den Ölmarkt zu stabilisieren.

zeit.title: Gewalttat in Frankreich: Was wir über den mutmaßlichen rassistischen Anschlag in Paris wissen
zeit.description: Ein Mann feuert nahe Paris mit einer automatischen Waffe auf Menschen. Ein Mann stirbt, vier Passanten werden verletzt. Was wir über die Tat wissen und was nicht.

zeit.title: Cynthia Fleury: »In der Gewalt zeigt sich Rache«
zeit.description: Jugend gegen Staat, Plünderer gegen Liberale: Für die Philosophin und Psychoanalytikerin Cynthia Fleury zeigt sich in den derzeitigen Protesten die Spaltung Frankreichs.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Handelsstreit: USA passen einige Kanada-Zölle nach Druck aus grenznahen Gliedstaaten an
nzz.description: Diesen Februar hat der Supreme Court Trumps Zölle für unrechtmässig erklärt. Doch der amerikanische Präsident verursacht mit seinen umstrittenen Zöllen weiter weltweit Turbulenzen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Krise bei Volkswagen: VW will auch über die Eröffnung von Transfergesellschaften verhandeln
nzz.description: Der Volkswagen-Konzern steht vor einem einschneidenden Umbau. Bis 2030 wird Europas grösster Autobauer 50 000 weitere Stellen abbauen. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: Macron spricht von einem «terroristischen und rassistischen Angriff»: mindestens ein Toter und fünf Verletzte nach Schüssen im Grossraum Paris
nzz.description: Unter den Verletzten ist auch ein zwölfjähriges Kind. Der mutmassliche Täter wurde festgenommen.

nzz.title: Nachfolge von Guy Parmelin: Die SVP liefert skurrile Episoden und lässt eine entscheidende Frage offen
nzz.description: Lange Zeit war Céline Amaudruz die einzige Bundesratskandidatin. Dann kam der Freitagmorgen – und mit ihm eine Welle von weiteren Kandidaten. Rückblick auf eine denkwürdige Kandidatensuche.

nzz.title: Debakel um den Kampfjet F-35: Der Bundesrat gelobt Besserung – aber mit Einschränkungen
nzz.description: Der Bundesrat nimmt 6 der 7 Empfehlungen der Geschäftsprüfer des Nationalrats vollständig an. Bei einem Punkt geht der Bundesrat auf Distanz.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Proteste in Frankreich: Die Regierung mobilisiert für die angekündigten Demos am Samstag 70 000 Polizisten
nzz.description: Seit Ende September gehen Schüler, Lehrpersonen und Gewerkschaften auf die Strasse – und lösen eine landesweite Bewegung aus, die zu Krawallen und Gewalt führt. Die neusten Entwicklungen.

nzz.title: «Bismillah, c’est les ténèbres» – wie ein sinnfreier Spruch zum Slogan des französischen Protests wurde
nzz.description: Er ist überall, auf Plakaten, in Chats, gerufen auf der Strasse. Auf Deutsch heisst der Protestruf der jungen Franzosen «Im Namen Gottes, es ist die Finsternis». Ein semantischer Unsinn. Was nur hat die Polizei damit zu tun und was die Meme-Kultur?

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN WIRTSCHAFT - Der Bund gibt 45 Millionen Liter Diesel aus Pflichtlagern frei +++ UBS gewinnt laut Medienbericht Rechtsstreit gegen ehemalige CS-Manager in New York
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus der Wirtschaft.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Melania Trump vermittelt Waffenruhe in besetzter Frontstadt Oleschki +++ Starlink läuft in der Ukraine offenbar weiterhin nur gedrosselt
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: «Wir machen euch fertig»: El Salvadors starker Mann legt sich mit haitianischen Banden an
nzz.description: Nayib Bukele ist das grosse Vorbild der neuen Rechten in Lateinamerika. Jetzt sendet er Soldaten nach Haiti, um entführte Landsleute zu befreien.

nzz.title: Der Preis des Meistertitels: Der FC Thun saniert mit Transfers die Finanzen, verliert aber den Glanz des Ausserordentlichen
nzz.description: Die klammen Berner Oberländer nehmen dank Spielerverkäufen netto über 10 Millionen Franken ein. Doch die Erneuerung kostet sie Niederlagen und emotionale Substanz. Und sie steht für eine belastende Zerreissprobe.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Mehr Staat, mehr Steuern, mehr Dilettantismus: Deutschlands Finanzpolitik schadet dem Standort
nzz.description: Finanzminister Lars Klingbeil ersinnt am laufenden Band neue Steuern und mästet den Staat. Dabei braucht Deutschland das Gegenteil: weniger Staat und weniger Abgaben. Es ist höchste Zeit für eine finanzpolitische Kurskorrektur.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Auch Griechenland verbietet soziale Netzwerke für Jugendliche. Ist das technisch überhaupt machbar? Und was sagt die Forschung über solche Verbote?
nzz.description: Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten zu Altersgrenzen bei sozialen Netzwerken.

nzz.title: Wenn die Zeit für eine Stunde stillsteht
nzz.description: Neugeborene Zwillinge tauschen das Alter, die Polizei verdächtigt die Falschen – was während der Zeitumstellung am Wochenende passieren könnte.

observador.title: Estado Novo tem centro interpretativo em Santa Comba Dão
observador.description: Inaugurado na Escola Cantina Salazar, em Santa Comba Dão, o espaço tem coordenação científica da Ephemera. Secretário de Estado diz que "estudar a ditadura é uma responsabilidade da democracia".

observador.title: OE2027. Carneiro justifica viabilização com crises mundiais
observador.description: O líder do PS justificou a decisão com o custo de vida dos portugueses e a instabilidade em Espanha, França, Alemanha, EUA e Brasil. "Portugal em primeiro lugar", disse.

observador.title: PS não pede demissão do presidente do IHRU
observador.description: O líder do PS reconheceu que as declarações de Benjamim Pereira foram infelizes, mas recusou tomar partido sobre a sua saída. BE exige demissão.

observador.title: 23h. Presidente do IHRU. Líder do PS diz que é decisão do PM
observador.description: O secretário-geral do PS fala em declarações infelizes de Benjamim Pereira. Ainda, já terminou a acampada de apoio a uma viúva com dois filhos que está a ser despejada, em Lisboa.

observador.title: Gasolina terá descida acentuada na próxima semana
observador.description: O ACP estimava uma queda de oito cêntimos por litro, mas a subida do ISP e o efeito do IVA vão atenuar o alívio. Brent atinge 117 dólares, máximo desde abril.

observador.title: Sondagens não dão maioria nem a Netanyahu nem à oposição
observador.description: Nenhuma dos blocos de partidos atinge o número mínimo para a maioria absoluta (61 deputados), segundo as três derradeiras sondagens com vista às eleições legislativas de 27 de outubro.

observador.title: Acampada do Porto nega contactos com Pedro Duarte
observador.description: Porta-voz da Acampada não tem dúvidas que Pedro Duarte quer "provocar alguma dissonância" e pede ao autarca que fale com o movimento "em vez de procurar pontos de rutura".

observador.title: Governo tenta polarizar? Neves quis mostrar que é o xerife?
observador.description: Em semana de acampadas e reações políticas ao tema da habitação, os ases do Fora do Baralho discutem a postura do Governo e do Presidente da República.

observador.title: Protestos continuam em Évora no sábado e dia 30
observador.description: Assembleia popular decidiu mudar local das manifestações para a "sala de visitas" da cidade. Protestos acontecem às 18h00 de sábado e a 30 de outubro.

observador.title: 22h. PR vai pressionar partidos a entendimentos na Habitação
observador.description: António José Seguro aponta duas dimensões: quer medidas urgentes e quer políticas duradouras. E ainda,  Acampada do Porto negou contactos classificados por Pedro Duarte como "muito cordiais".

observador.title: Viseu une-se à luta pelo direito à habitação
observador.description: Pouco mais de 100 pessoas ligadas a diversas associações juntaram-se esta sexta-feira na rua Formosa, em Viseu. Assembleia popular levou três documentos a votação, todos aprovados por unanimidade.

observador.title: ​Ainda as falhas no Starlink e mais apoio escandinavo
observador.description: Imprensa ucraniana aborda reforço do apoio à Ucrânia vindo da Finlândia. Admite ainda que há falhas na forma como Starlink está a ser usado no país.

observador.title: ​Rússia congratula-se com avanços na linha da frente
observador.description: Imprensa russa dá eco a avanços na linha da frente anunciados pelo governo russo. Destacam ainda troca de prisioneiros com a Ucrânia.

observador.title: Evangélicos e católicos lutam pelo voto no Brasil
observador.description: Na igreja evangélica onde vai Michelle Bolsonaro, o pastor não esconde a preferência por Flávio. Em São Paulo, um padre faz obra social e aproveita para evangelizar sobre Lula.

observador.title: MAI. Chega quer ouvir António Costa e mais de 50 pessoas
observador.description: Da lista constam ex-PMs, ministros, juízes, jornalistas e empresários. André Ventura preside à comissão, que se reúne segunda e terça-feira.

observador.title: Estudo sugere que Meta cobrou mais à campanha de Lula
observador.description: Investigação do NetLab sugere que o PT pagou entre 33% e 43% mais por anúncios na Meta do que o PL, mas revisão metodológica não confirma diferença significativa.

observador.title: Cheques psicólogo: ministério nega atrasos nos pagamentos
observador.description: O Governo garantiu que as consultas que ultrapassaram os 90 dias foram pagas, um dia depois de um grupo de psicólogos ter denunciado a falta de pagamento. 3.875 psicólogos aderiram a este programa.

observador.title: Turquia julga Netanyahu à revelia por flotilha
observador.description: Tribunal de Istambul acusa 35 líderes israelitas de crimes contra a humanidade e genocídio. Procuradoria pede penas que podem somar 4.600 anos de prisão.

spiegel.title: Kenia: Mehrere Vermisste nach Einsturz von Hochhaus in Nairobi
spiegel.description: In Kenias Hauptstadt Nairobi ist ein Hochhaus eingestürzt. Sieben Menschen werden noch immer vermisst. Örtliche Medien berichten von Plünderungen.

spiegel.title: Laura Owens: Frau erfindet Schwangerschaft nach Nacht mit Ex-»Bachelor«
spiegel.description: Eine Frau hat nach einer Nacht mit dem ehemaligen »Bachelor« behauptet, er sei der Vater ungeborener Zwillinge – obwohl sie nie Geschlechtsverkehr hatten. Der Mann wehrte sich erfolgreich. Er war nicht ihr einziges Opfer.

spiegel.title: Handelsstreit mit Kanada: USA lockern Zölle gegen landwirtschaftliche Produkte
spiegel.description: US-Staaten an der Grenze zu Kanada leiden unter den hohen Zöllen gegen Produkte aus dem Nachbarland. Nun hat die Regierung einige Ausnahmen beschlossen – wohl auch wegen Kritik aus der eigenen Partei.

spiegel.title: Markus Söder: Wie das Aigner-Dilemma seine Kanzlerträume gefährden könnte
spiegel.description: Die CSU will Ilse Aigner als Bundespräsidentin, Parteichef Markus Söder muss sie unterstützen – auch wenn das seine Kanzlerträume zunichtemachen könnte. Vielleicht kommt ihm jetzt ausgerechnet Friedrich Merz zu Hilfe.

spiegel.title: American Football: Neues »Retro«-Logo der Atlanta Falcons erinnert Fans an Nazisymbolik
spiegel.description: Ein schwarzer Vogel, goldene Streifen, roter Hintergrund – das alles in »Retro-Optik«. Fans der Atlanta Falcons kommentieren unter dem Logo des NFL-Teams einen Nazivergleich nach dem anderen.

spiegel.title: Bayern-Trainer: Vincent Kompany nach Zusammenbruch in stabilem Zustand
spiegel.description: Er sah gerade beim Training der zweiten Mannschaft zu, dann brach er zusammen. Bayern-Coach Vincent Kompany wurde ins Krankenhaus eingeliefert. Sein Zustand soll stabil sein.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Emmanuel Macron besucht Pariser Vorort nach tödlichen Schüssen
spiegel.description: Nach Schüssen bei Paris ist ein Mensch tot, vier weitere sind verletzt. Der Bürgermeister der betroffenen Gemeinde vermutet ein islamfeindliches Motiv. Präsident Macron drückt vor Ort Anteilnahme aus.

spiegel.title: Midterms in Alaska: US-Justizministerium reicht Klage wegen doppeltem Dan Sullivan ein
spiegel.description: Kandidiert Dan J. Sullivan nur, um Dan S. Sullivan die Stimmen zu stehlen? Davon geht offenbar die US-Regierung aus. Um das zu verhindern, hat das Justizministerium nun rechtliche Schritte eingeleitet.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz: Erstmals reist ein »Nius«-Mitarbeiter im Regierungsflieger mit
spiegel.description: Das Portal »Nius« ist für seine Rechts-außen-Kampagnen bekannt. Bei bisherigen Reisen von Kanzler Friedrich Merz war das Medium in der Regierungsmaschine nicht dabei. Das hat sich nun geändert.

spiegel.title: Darline Graham: Donald Trump verrät ihren Bruder Lindsey – fünf Tage später macht sie Wahlkampf mit ihm
spiegel.description: Lindsey Graham war der wichtigste Ukrainefreund in Trumps Lager. Seine Schwester erbte den Senatssitz. Nun kippt Trump die Russlandsanktionen, die den Namen ihres Bruders tragen. Und Darline Graham? Umgarnt den Präsidenten.

spiegel.title: Daniel Aminati: Was Patrice Aminatis Krebserkrankung mit ihrer Scheidung zu tun hat
spiegel.description: Seit drei Jahren lebt die Influencerin Patrice Aminati mit der Diagnose Hautkrebs – und seit einem Jahr ohne ihren Ex-Mann Daniel Aminati. In einem Interview sprach sie nun erstmals über das Ende der Beziehung.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Russland-Krieg: Melania Trump verkündet lokale Waffenruhe verkünden, Kreml und Kyjiw bestätigen
spiegel.description: Im ukrainischen Oleschky droht eine humanitäre Katastrophe. Nun teilt das Weiße Haus mit, dass Melania Trump eine lokale Waffenruhe vermittelt habe. Es solle eine Evakuierung der Zivilbevölkerung ermöglicht werden.

spiegel.title: Israel: Wie Benjamin Netanyahu trotz Skandalen an der Macht bleibt
spiegel.description: Eine Affäre um Katar, ein Korruptionsprozess, das Versagen am 7. Oktober: Benjamin Netanyahu hat vor dieser Wahl viel überstanden. Was ihn an der Macht hält – und warum seine Gegner ihn so schwer ablösen können.

spiegel.title: Jordanien: Mehrere Menschen sterben nach Angriff auf Kirche
spiegel.description: Bei Schüssen auf Teilnehmer eines Trauerzugs sind in Jordanien mindestens sechs Menschen getötet und 28 verletzt worden. König Abdullah II. bezeichnete die Tat als »Terroranschlag«.

spiegel.title: Bayern-Trainer: Vincent Kompany in Klinik gebracht
spiegel.description: Vincent Kompany ist in einer Klinik. Der Coach des FC Bayern München hatte vergangene Woche mit einer Virusinfektion zu kämpfen. Nun teilte der Verein mit, dass er während eines Trainings zusammengebrochen ist.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Datenleak bei der AfD, Markus Söder, Gewalt in Frankreich
spiegel.description: Eine ausgestanden geglaubte Spendenaffäre holt die AfD-Chefin ein. Ilse Aigner ist der Star des CSU-Parteitags. Ein tödlicher Angriff trifft Frankreich in ohnehin angespannter Situation. Das ist die Lage am Freitagabend.

spiegel.title: Moskau: Flughafen Scheremetjewo nach Drohnen-Alarm evakuiert
spiegel.description: Russlands größter Airport hat zeitweise den Betrieb einstellen müssen. Nach einem Drohnenalarm brachten Mitarbeitende ihre Kollegen und Fluggäste in Sicherheit – nicht zum ersten Mal.

spiegel.title: Buchclub in Frankreich: Wie junge Männer aus dem Banlieue Klassiker neu entdecken
spiegel.description: Junge Männer aus dem Banlieue gründen in einem Hinterhof einen Buchclub. Und machen ausgerechnet aus Klassikern Social-Media-Content. Kann das funktionieren?

letemps.title: Miki, la plante pop qui ne cesse de grandir
letemps.description:
Ses détracteurs l’ont (trop) vite qualifiée d'«industry plant», terme désignant des stars soi-disant fabriquées de toutes pièces par l’industrie. Depuis, la Franco-coréenne a sorti un album et leur a donné tort. Confirmation le 4 novembre à l’Alhambra de Genève

C’est l’histoire d’une plante qui a poussé vite. Qui a eu de l’eau et surtout, beaucoup de lumière, pour faire sa photosynthèse.

phys-org.description: Researchers at AIST have directly observed magnetic flux quanta generated in a superconductor by photon absorption and demonstrated a new principle of photon detection that identifies the number of photons based on the number of these flux quanta.

phys-org.description: The new RFD4-Proteina unified generative model for protein design—created by the Institute for Protein Design (IPD) in collaboration with NVIDIA—uses advanced AI to generate entirely new protein sequences and structures, achieving computational design success rates five to 10 times higher than previous models and generating candidates five to 10 times faster.

phys-org.description: Researchers at AIST have demonstrated the synthesis of nanoporous carbonaceous materials and carbonaceous materials with layered nanostructures through a simple process involving the chemical modification of common sugars such as sucrose and fructose.

phys-org.title: The psychology of why we overpay for used cars—study points to left-digit bias

phys-org.title: Designing better adsorbents to remove PFAS from water
phys-org.description: A review by Tohoku University researchers identifies key molecular features that could guide the development of more effective materials for removing PFAS from water. The study is published in the journal ACS Materials Au.

phys-org.description: In 1953, two physicists showed that an electron beam skimming past a grating emits light whose color depends only on the electron's speed and the grating's spacing. Known as Smith-Purcell radiation, this phenomenon has become a useful tool for building compact, tunable light sources and tracking particle beams without touching them.

But new research shows that congressional elections follow strong statistical patterns, even when individual races produce surprises.

phys-org.description: Many of the most potent antibiotics originate from bacteria. A large proportion belong to a class of compounds known as nonribosomal peptides (NRP). They are produced by large bacterial enzyme machineries—the nonribosomal peptide synthetases, or NRPS for short. These function like molecular assembly lines: Similar to the stations in a car factory, where new parts are added to the car at each step, several specialized modules string together amino acid by amino acid to build a peptide.

phys-org.title: New marker panel and free web tool help track stem cells as they develop
phys-org.description: How can the identity of pluripotent stem cells be determined more reliably during their differentiation? Researchers from the IUF—Leibniz Research Institute for Environmental Medicine and Heinrich Heine University Duesseldorf have systematically validated marker genes for this purpose and developed a web-based application for the automated classification of early cell fates. The study has been published in Stem Cell Reports.

phys-org.title: Can we stop antibiotic resistance from ruining promising drugs before they reach patients?
phys-org.description: What if we could predict early in drug development which antibiotics bacteria are most likely to become resistant to? In a review published in Nature Reviews Microbiology, researchers from the HUN-REN Biological Research Centre, Szeged (HUN-REN BRC Szeged) and the Hungarian Centre of Excellence for Molecular Medicine (HCEMM) in Szeged propose a five-step decision-making framework that could help identify resistance risks early, refine promising drug candidates and prevent costly failures.

phys-org.title: Potatoes could be the secret to better plant-based meat, say food scientists

phys-org.title: Everyday Mylar turned into a promising insulator for lunar habitats

phys-org.title: Chaos makes sense of market movements in a crisis
phys-org.description: Research shows that crises do more than cause financial market volatility and falling share prices—they lead to markets becoming far more interconnected.

phys-org.title: Stellar collision may explain why Orion Nebula's planet-forming disks appear younger than its stars
phys-org.description: The Orion Nebula is a large star-forming region visible to the naked eye. Some of the young stars in the nebula are surrounded by disks of gas and dust in which planets form. Radiation from the massive central star, 1 Ori C1 (Theta-1 Orionis C1), gradually strips material from these disks, giving them shapes that resemble tadpoles.

phys-org.title: Scientists uncover the molecular pillars that shape our cells' powerpacks
phys-org.description: Mitochondria are the tiny powerpacks that supply most of the energy our cells need. Their ability to generate this energy relies on a distinctive architecture: two membranes, one tucked inside the other, separated by a narrow gap called the intermembrane space (IMS). This tiny space helps sustain the chemistry of energy production, making its organization critical to how these cellular powerpacks function.

phys-org.title: Mechanism behind PARP1-mediated DNA repair characterized, offering insight into targeted cancer therapy
phys-org.description: When DNA is damaged, cellular processes respond and repair the DNA. Inhibiting DNA damage repair can be therapeutically beneficial in cancers with genetic vulnerabilities related to DNA damage response. Scientists at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital have uncovered a mechanism behind how this process works, which may have implications for cancer treatment. The results were published today in Molecular Cell.

proj-syn.description: If current trends continue, the Chinese state will find itself exposed to a political succession crisis, a weakening economy, and a lack of resources to exercise power domestically and project it externally. It would be a perfect storm, with far-reaching global repercussions.

This is true of the global trading system, which has proven surprisingly resilient in recent years, and of the European economy, which might not have a tech giant to rival those in the US or China, but remains a global trade powerhouse and a leader in science and research. While Europe has much to do to improve its external competitiveness, it must not ac

proj-syn.title: Who Pays the Fiscal Watchdogs?
proj-syn.description: Civil-society oversight is the cheapest insurance in sovereign finance, because it enables independent scrutiny long before a default. But given that a borrowing government will never volunteer to fund the people who audit it, global decision-makers must do so using agreements for stolen-asset recovery and sovereign-debt treatments.

proj-syn.title: How to Help Left-Behind Regions
proj-syn.description: Pouring public investment into poorer towns and cities might be politically beneficial, but the economic returns of indiscriminate largesse would be limited. A better approach would concentrate investment in areas with the potential to become high-productivity hubs, such as large peripheral cities.

proj-syn.title: The Agentic Information Economy
proj-syn.description: An internet populated and run by AI agents will need not just reliable data but also a broader information ecology capable of questioning its own inputs and transmitting corrections where they are needed if information changes. But whether this will serve private interests or the public good remains to be seen.

proj-syn.title: A Competitive Europe Must Be Climate-Resilient
proj-syn.description: Extreme weather and climate-related events caused €822 billion in economic losses across the European Union between 1980 and 2024, with a quarter of the losses occurring just in the last five years. The consequences for Europe’s competitiveness and economic security are clear—and so is the appropriate response.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Prepare for the Worst
proj-syn.description: Those seeking to weaken the EU’s supranational foundations are already preparing their radical schemes, like the “new deal for Europe” that Germany's Alternative für Deutschland recently presented in the European Parliament. The pro-EU camp must be prepared with new political strategies and institutional arrangements.

proj-syn.title: Nature Can’t Wait
proj-syn.description: Although the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine are spurring governments to increase spending on defense and focus more on economic growth, it would be a mistake to postpone investments designed to protect nature. In fact, meeting internationally agreed targets could add up to $450 billion to annual global GDP by 2050.

proj-syn.title: Argentina’s Economic Chainsaw Massacre
proj-syn.description: Argentine President Javier Milei may currently be a lynchpin in US President Donald Trump’s geoeconomic vision for Latin America; but he could soon become its weak link. With elections coming next year, he has achieved an economic recovery and relative price stability by driving millions of his people into destitution.

proj-syn.title: Which AI Myth Will We Embrace?
proj-syn.description: The mythos—or foundational stories—that we tell ourselves will determine our fate in the age of AI. As industry leaders regale us with utopian visions of benevolent digital gods delivering scientific breakthroughs and expanding our technological horizons, our best defense against hubris is a counternarrative of social cooperation.

proj-syn.title: No More Superpowers
proj-syn.description: Although the United States remains very powerful and Russia still commands enormous conventional and nuclear capabilities, each country’s global status has come to be defined by failure and constraint. If anything, both may belong to the same broad grouping of middle powers that includes the likes of Canada, Brazil, and India.

proj-syn.title: What’s Driving Persistent Inflation?
proj-syn.description: In their preoccupation with high public debt, rising bond yields, and dizzying AI valuations, investors have seemingly forgotten the supply shocks shaping the underlying inflation outlook. But anyone worried about debt and yields must reckon with the disruptions created in the name of protecting domestic markets.

proj-syn.title: Building the Economy Africa Needs
proj-syn.description: Africa cannot control global geopolitics, let alone prevent external shocks. But it can manage its exposure, especially by building an integrated continental market, investing in higher-value-added production, and pushing for reform of the global credit-rating agencies.

proj-syn.title: Science Without Scientists?
proj-syn.description: Now that autonomous systems are capable of generating their own hypotheses, designing experiments, and writing up the results, the scientific community must adapt. For scientific knowledge to retain its standing, its sources must be trusted and answerable to the public.

proj-syn.title: When Smart Cities Turn Menacing
proj-syn.description: Uganda has embraced digital-surveillance tools in the name of improving public safety and combating terrorism, a pattern that is repeating itself across several African countries. But governments are increasingly using these technologies for political control, rather than for national security.

proj-syn.title: Brazil Cannot Afford Bolsonaro’s Spending Cuts
proj-syn.description: If he wins the October 25 runoff, far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro plans to slash public spending by as much as 1.5% of GDP. These cuts could push Brazil into recession, hurt workers and small businesses, and drain tax revenue—all without solving the country’s debt problem.

proj-syn.title: A Generational Reckoning on the Streets of Paris
proj-syn.description: As their schools deteriorate and the planet grows hotter, many young people in France do not have hope for a decent future. The recent protests may foreshadow a broader conflict between older generations who wield political power and younger people who must live in the world they leave behind.

proj-syn.title: The Algorithm Driving French Student Protests
proj-syn.description: One of the main drivers of the student protests in France is the opposition to Parcoursup, the country’s university-admissions platform, which is widely denounced as opaque and unfair. While such automated decision-making systems do not create educational inequalities, they can exacerbate them.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI Drives A Varied Lineup Of Large Financings
crunchbase.description: It was another interesting week for AI-related startup funding, with a number of large rounds and quirky companies. The largest financings went to Tenstorrent, a developer of AI processors and systems, and AI lab Flapping Airplanes. The quirkiest round, meanwhile, was undoubtedly a $200 million financing for Warhound, which wants to breed elite military dogs. A number of big rounds in areas including biotech, space tech and physical AI rounded out the list.

In this guest commentary, Seth Kugler, a partner at Grellas Shah LLP, warns companies that they should adopt strict AI policies, restrict data access on unmanaged devices, update confidentiality agreements, and act immediately when misuse is suspected.

crunchbase.title: The AI IPO Wave Is The Dot-Com Bubble’s Evil Twin. Anthropic’s Delay Just Proved It.
crunchbase.description: In this guest article from Airrived co-founder and CEO Anurag Gurtu, he contends that Anthropic’s rapid revenue growth does not justify its proposed $2 trillion IPO valuation, given enormous infrastructure commitments, safety concerns, customer concentration and competition from cheaper open-weight models, saying instead that lasting enterprise AI value will come from proprietary data, reliable deployment and measurable customer outcomes rather than expensive models alone.

crunchbase.title: Acquirers Are Snapping Up Boom-Era Startups That Haven’t Raised Funding In Years
crunchbase.description: A number of companies whose names might feature on a playlist of 2021 boom-era unicorns have sold to acquirers in recent months, including one-time highfliers like Airtable, Headspace and Miro. In many cases, companies are selling at valuations which, while not puny, are still far below their former peaks.

crunchbase.title: Your Next Customer Might Be An Agent. Here’s How To Build Your Brand For Both Humans And AI.
crunchbase.description: As AI agents increasingly recommend and purchase products, brands must appeal to both machines and humans by documenting their voice, creating clear product descriptions and checking how AI summarizes their messaging. Guest author Toby Coulthard suggests that startups should build these practices in from the outset, preserving human appeal while measuring success through conversions and revenue rather than content volume.

crunchbase.title: When A Startup Sells, Its Employees’ Equity Plans Can Change Overnight
crunchbase.description: Startup acquisitions can reshape employees’ finances and careers, with individual outcomes depending on a variety of conditions. Guest author Ron Honig, co-CEO and managing partner of From-Honig Family Office, suggests that before making major life changes, employees should clarify their award rights, when proceeds will become available, and what their after-tax payout can realistically support.

crunchbase.title: ‘Weird And Maybe Uninvestable’: How Reach Capital Spots Its Venture Winners
crunchbase.description: Crunchbase News spoke with James Kim, partner at Reach Capital, about how Reach’s education roots inform its broader strategy, what it saw in AI detection company GPTZero, and why some of its best investments initially divided its own team. We also discussed how ownership stakes and secondary transactions have shaped the firm’s approach to returning capital.
